# T6.13: libnvencvt for every app

The overlay now enables the encoder for every process (`NVMTL_NVENCVT=1`) instead of a list (Parsec, OBS, ffmpeg,
Sunshine). That moves two things from "only Parsec" to "every Metal app": the cost of registering, and requests the
encoder cannot meet.

## Registration cost

The plugin loads `libnvencvt.dylib` and calls `NVEncVT_Register` while it creates the Metal device, in every process
it is enabled for. The GPU check used an RM client and the class list: 6-9 ms (plus ~0.6 ms to load the library in a
GUI app). Now it reads the GPU's PCI device ID from the IORegistry: Ada (AD102-AD107) is 0x2600-0x28ff. Load +
register: **~1.5 ms** (was 12-20 ms in a GUI-like process). The RM class list remains the fallback when the registry
has no NVIDIA device.

## Requests the encoder cannot meet

- `tools/avwrite.m` (new): writes a moving pattern through AVAssetWriter, the path most apps use, reads it back and
  compares. H.264 and HEVC at 640x360, 1280x720, 1920x1080 and 3840x2160 use our encoder and read back correctly
  (stats log; AVFoundation encodes in the app's process here).
- **HEVC Main10** (10-bit input, `kVTProfileLevel_HEVC_Main10_AutoLevel`): VideoToolbox converts the frames to our
  NV12 and our encoder writes 8-bit Main; Apple's software encoder would write Main10. AVFoundation ignores a refused
  `ProfileLevel` and does not pass the profile in the encoder specification, so this cannot be steered away from us.
  What changed: the encoder registers `SupportedSelectionProperties` = {ProfileLevel: the profiles it can produce}
  (H.264 Baseline/Main/High at every level, HEVC Main), like Apple's HEVC encoder, so apps that select by profile get
  Apple's encoder for anything else, and `SetProperty(ProfileLevel)` refuses unlisted profiles
  (`kVTPropertyNotSupportedErr`) instead of accepting them silently. Real Main10 needs 10-bit support in the encoder
  (Ada NVENC has it): open.
- No B-frames (`AllowFrameReordering` is accepted and ignored, the stream has none), as before.
